source.title: The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overparameterization
source.authors: Jonas von Berg; Adalbert Fono; Massimiliano Datres; Sohir Maskey; G. Kutyniok

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper sweeps network width and measures stability and test performance in near-interpolating networks, conceptually testing whether wider networks continue to generalize. It does not test random-label memorization or weight-space sharpness.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds and width-sweep experiments. Rows below capture the reported experimental outcomes that bear on V2; cited prior-work results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports increasing test accuracy with width for near-interpolating 8-layer CIFAR-10 MLPs, bearing on V2 in a new architecture and training setting. Its stability measures alone do not test V2 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the empirical conclusions: stability generally rises with width, qualitatively tracks CIFAR-10 MLP test accuracy, and is more informative there than standard weight norms. Training duration and Gaussian variance qualify stability scaling. The central theoretical conclusion is that, under the stated assumptions, substantial overparameterization is necessary for combining strong fitting with high robustness; sufficiency remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies stability and generalization bounds and reports width sweeps; it does not reproduce the one-hidden-layer ReLU experiments described in V2. Experimental models use 4 or 8 layers, and training uses Adam for embedding and output layers and Muon for hidden layers.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration changes the MNIST 8-layer stability trend; increasing Gaussian variance disrupts monotonic stability-width scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Class stability and normalized co-stability generally increase with width; MNIST training duration and Gaussian variance alter that relationship.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization is associated with greater input-space robustness under specified training and data conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under concentration and hypothesis-class assumptions, the paper derives stability-dependent generalization bounds and necessary parameter capacity for simultaneously fitting and remaining robust.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stable near-interpolation requires substantial overparameterization under the stated assumptions; this does not establish monotonically improving test error with width.

record.problems: The experiments report near-interpolation (at least 99% training accuracy), not zero training error or a measured interpolation threshold. Most width-trend results are qualitative; individual plotted values are not stated in the text. The paper reports CIFAR-10 MLP test accuracy around 50%, far below the Bayes optimum, and states that the Gaussian-data behavior needs broader width and dataset evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported width-sweep results were omitted.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label fitting and held-out accuracy.

Continued test-error improvement beyond an established zero-training-error threshold; training to convergence; the original one-hidden-layer unregularized setting. Other sweeps report stability without corresponding test-error trends.
Convolutional-versus-fully-connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent generalization differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other gap-ranking measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Stability reversals cannot support limits_scope or challenges verdicts on V2. Input-space margins and normalized score margins also do not measure V7's magnitude-aware weight-space sharpness. No precise plotted values are recoverable from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments reach at least 99% training accuracy rather than explicitly reporting zero training error; they do not locate the interpolation threshold or test error beyond it. No MNIST or CIFAR-10 row compares a width sweep with random-label training.

rows.value: Class stability increases with width; the paper says the increase aligns with the qualitative trend in test performance.

rows.value: Both stability measures increase with width and follow the same qualitative trend as test accuracy.

rows.note: The configuration with w = 128 was excluded because it failed to attain 99% training accuracy after 400 epochs. Test accuracy is reported in text as around 50%.
rows.check: Section 6 explicitly says test accuracy follows the increasing width trend. Retain that qualitative accuracy result separately from stability. The retained widths are 256–2048; width 128 failed the training-accuracy criterion and was excluded. Zero training error and convergence are not established.
